Indonesian Metals Sector Sees Boost as Pacific Alloy Resources Announces $400 Million Smelter Project

Indonesia’s metals and mining industry received a significant vote of confidence this week after Pacific Alloy Resources revealed plans to invest $400 million in a new nickel smelting facility in Central Sulawesi. The project, slated to begin construction in the third quarter of 2024, is expected to bolster Indonesia’s position as a leading global producer of battery-grade nickel, a vital component in the fast-growing electric vehicle supply chain.

Company officials said the new smelter, with an initial annual processing capacity of 30,000 metric tons of nickel, will employ up to 1,200 workers during construction and create around 600 permanent jobs upon completion in 2026. “This investment underscores our long-term commitment to Indonesia and its critical role in the global energy transition,” said Pacific Alloy Resources CEO Agus Santoso at a press briefing in Jakarta on Thursday. “We are working closely with local authorities to ensure the project aligns with sustainability and community development goals.”

Government officials welcomed the announcement as part of Indonesia’s broader strategy to move up the metals value chain. “We are pleased to see new investment in downstream processing, which supports our vision of developing an integrated battery industry,” said Diah Puspita, director of downstream industry at the Ministry of Industry. “Such projects generate employment, transfer technology, and increase export value.”

Industry analysts said the move reflects robust demand for Indonesian nickel, as automakers and battery manufacturers worldwide seek secure supplies of key raw materials. “Indonesia’s policy to restrict raw ore exports has driven companies to invest locally,” noted Edwin Halim, an analyst at Nusantara Capital Advisors. “We expect further announcements as global demand for EV batteries accelerates.”

According to the Indonesian Nickel Association, the country accounted for over 45% of global nickel production in 2023. The new smelter is expected to add significant capacity to the sector and further solidify Indonesia’s role in the global metals market.
